facts.content: 3-day history of diarrhea.
Reports 4–5 bowel movements per day, watery to loose consistency.
Experiences mild intermittent abdominal pain.
Experienced one episode of vomiting.
Denies presence of blood or mucus.
Possible low-grade fever reported.
Reports decreased appetite but maintains oral fluid intake.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient states taking Lexapro and mentions an unclear yellow inhaler.
No known drug allergies.
Father had hypertension.
Father died of bowel cancer at age 62, approximately 10 years ago.
facts.source_text: father died of bowel CA at 62 (~10 yrs ago)

facts.content: Assessment is acute diarrhea, likely self-limited gastroenteritis.
facts.source_text: Acute diarrhea, likely self-limited gastroenteritis: 3 days, 4–5/day, no blood/mucus, tolerating fluids; single emesis; mild abdo pain; possible low-grade fever

facts.content: History of asthma noted in assessment.
Encourage fluid intake and use oral rehydration salts like Dioralyte as needed.
facts.source_text: Hydration: Encourage fluids; oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) PRN

facts.content: Recommended a soft diet initially, avoiding dairy, meat, and eggs.
facts.source_text: Diet: “Soft” diet—toast/crackers/jam; then boiled/mashed veg; avoid dairy, meat, eggs initially; probiotic yoghurt OK

facts.content: Advance diet after 48 hours without diarrhea before reintroducing meat, eggs, and fish.
facts.source_text: Advance diet after 48 hrs without diarrhea before reintroducing meat/eggs/fish

facts.content: Submit stool sample if diarrhea persists longer than a week or if blood is present.
facts.source_text: If diarrhea persists >1 week or any blood in stool → submit stool sample

facts.content: Seek urgent care if frequency increases to 6–8 times per day or signs of dehydration appear.
facts.source_text: if frequency increases to ≥6–8/day or signs of dehydration → seek urgent care/hospital

facts.content: Return if symptoms worsen or for any concerns.
